newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU directive to help lawyers practice abroad.
newsitem.headline: EU directive to help lawyers practice abroad.

text.p: European Union internal market ministers are expected to agree on Wednesday rules to make it easier for lawyers to set up a permanent practice elsewhere in the Union, EU diplomats said on Tuesday.
The proposed EU directive aims to facilitate the practice of the profession of lawyer in other EU member states than in the one where the lawyer was qualified.

If adopted, lawyers could either practice under their home-country professional title for an unlimited period or seek admission to the profession of lawyer in the concerned member state after a transitional period of three years.

A lawyer working under his home-country professional title could carry out the same activities as a colleague from that member state. He/she could give advice on the law of his home member state, on EU law, on international law and on the law of the host country.
Luxembourg had voiced reservations about the proposal but diplomats still expected Wednesday's meeting to adopt a common position, which would then need the approval of the European Parliament.
Lawyers who just want to provide services in another member state may already do so under an EU law agreed twenty years ago.
As part of the drive to establish a single market, the EU also adopted legislation in 1988 on the recognition of higher-education diplomas in other member states.
However, under this directive member states may impose a test under on the applicant's knowledge of that country's law, in effect an obstacle to the freedom of establishment, diplomats said.
